title: 10 Limits and continuity: Visual Guide
outline: Title: 10 Limits and continuity — five interactive visuals, from the hole you already punch in a rational graph to the Intermediate Value Theorem

1. Hole Or Value | the cancelled factor of (x^2-9)/(x-3) beside the limit at x = 3: choose f(3) as undefined, as 2, or as 6, then shrink the approach distance h and watch the two-sided table close on 6 while a live three-box checklist tests continuity | the neighbourhood decides the limit and the single number f(3) decides continuity — they are separate questions

2. Both Sides Agree | a graph broken at x = 3 with draggable left and right arrival heights, one-sided limit pills, and a table whose gap column refuses to close as h shrinks from 1 to 0.001 | a two-sided limit exists only when both one-sided limits exist and match — never the sum, never the average, never the louder side

3. Cancel The Zero | five expressions each run through substitute-diagnose-fix: 0/0 cleared by factoring, a polynomial answered by substitution alone, c/0 with no cancellation available, and a root cleared by its conjugate, each with a live two-sided table | 0/0 is a diagnosis that the algebra is unfinished, never the answer 0, and c/0 with c non-zero is an asymptote instead

4. Which Law Is Real | six statements about f(x)=x+1 and g(x)=x^2 with a draggable approach point a: the left column measures the limit of the combined function, the right column combines the separate limits, and each row is tagged holds / fails / true at this a only | the three genuine laws hold at every a, the impostors swap + for x or / for -, and the quotient law goes grey at a = 0 where its condition is unmet

5. Every Value Between | five functions on fixed closed intervals with a draggable target height N: the panel reports continuity, whether N lies between f(a) and f(b), and bisects for the actual crossings — including 1/x on [-1,1], which changes sign without ever equalling zero | IVT trades continuity on a closed interval for existence only: no uniqueness, no location, no monotonicity, and no guarantee at all once a break is inside the interval
